core.title: Use the layer-to-default-action map for route sequences
core.given: A route sequence has steps assigned to the presentation, application, domain or integration layer
core.when: You define, select or check the default action for a layer in that sequence
core.then: Use the layer's default action: presentation → command, application → use_case, domain → validate, integration → persist.
prefer: Write steps in the <layer>.<default action> notation: presentation.command, application.use_case, domain.validate, integration.persist.
avoid: Giving a layer a different default action than the map assigns, for example making persist the domain default or validate the presentation default.
core.why: With one fixed layer-to-default-action map, every route sequence uses the same defaults, so sequences stay consistent and predictable.
evidence: Any default action stated or used for the presentation, application, domain or integration layer in the route sequence matches the map: command, use_case, validate, persist.
verification: Compare each layer's stated or applied default action in the route sequence with the layer-to-default-action map; a stated or applied default that differs from the map is a finding.
The check covers defaults only: a step that uses a non-default action is not a violation of this rule and must not be flagged, because the rule defines defaults and does not forbid other actions.

fires: A route sequence is being defined and a step for the presentation, application, domain or integration layer needs its default action.
A default action is being selected for a layer in a route sequence.
An existing route sequence's layer defaults are being checked or revised.
doesNotFire: Work that involves no route sequence and no layer-to-action mapping.
Edits to a sequence that change neither a step's layer nor its action (for example, prose wording fixes).

profileRequirements.meaning: Which layer roles a route sequence's steps are assigned to, and the stack's local names for them; the core's layer-to-default-action map is keyed by these layer roles.

bunOnly.text: Term layer_action: 'layer -> default action.' values: presentation=command, application=use_case, domain=validate, integration=persist.
bunOnly.reason: The term id layer_action and its term syntax are this realization's detector/term vocabulary; the neutral core states the same map as the obligation and describes the comparison generically in core.verification.

classification.note: The four layer names are role names; the stack's local layer names come from roles.layers.
Neutral as written; defines/selects/checks a layer's default action.
The map (presentation→command, application→use_case, domain→validate, integration→persist) is the obligation itself and names only roles and generic action names, so it stays in the core.
The <layer>.<default action> notation is the plan-artifact notation of the method, not a stack idiom; kept at role level.
Negative form of the map; the swapped-default examples are already role-level and neutral.
Neutral rationale (consistency and predictability of one fixed map).
Neutral: matches the map's stated or used defaults per layer role.

The generic check (compare each layer's stated or applied default with the map) and the scope exclusion (do not flag non-default actions) go to core:verification; the term id layer_action and its term text are realization details (bunOnly).

Task terms are the method's planner vocabulary (route sequence, layer, default action, layer role names); observable_now kept. The Bun note (task text mentions route sequences or the mapping) is implied by fact type task_term.

The neutral fact vocabulary has no 'layer' fact type, so it is expressed as fact type 'role' with the same values; llm_judged kept because layer attachment is read from the sequence text with no dedicated observer.

neutralityNotes: The convention is planner-method content: it names no stack, runtime, framework, language, path or file kind, so the core repeats the layer-to-default-action map verbatim (it is the obligation itself) and only the term id layer_action is realization-specific (bunOnly). The action names (command, use_case, validate, persist) are the method's default-action vocabulary, not stack idioms, so they stay in the core rather than the profile; the stack-varying part is only the layer roles' local names, supplied by roles.layers.
